page.layout: One page of text, full width. Above the text: printed page number 300 and a decorative border. Then the title (IN IESVITAM COR REGIS HENRICI IV. petentem.), followed by one verse poem (20 lines) and the closing word FINIS. No margin notes.

main_text.head: IN IESVITAM COR REGIS HENRICI IV. petentem.
main_text.p: QVEM nō mille manus, nō mille pericula mortis Quem nec & insidiis sternere quiuit Iber, Quem nequit Mars ipse ferox, fera sica peremit, Sica HENRICORVM sanguinolenta nece. Scilicet occubuit scelerata fraude petitus Arte, dolo, insidiis Rex, IVDAITA, tuis. Quid sceleris latuit tanti sub corde Monarchae, Vt scelerate tuo vulnere concideret? Sedibus eximiis te, & rursum in honore locauit, Dinitiisque[?] auxit, muneraque ampla dedit. Et plus quam par est, & sepe maiora tulisti, Gratia pro meritis haec referenda fuit? Vt cumulo adiiceret, proprio te CORDE beauit, Quid maius proprio quis dare CORDE potest? Nunc cape COR toties a te mucrone petitum, HARLÆVS votis annuit ipse tuis. Sed pariter cum DENTE, COR vt referatur eodē, Non sunt diuersis contumulanda locis Quæ Natura simul iunxit, quæ Parca reuulsit, Vsa instrumentis pestis amara tuis.

page.notes: Large initial Q of QVEM is a decorative woodcut-style capital, joined to the word. A dingbat-like mark follows "nece" at line end; not a reference, left out. "IVDAITA" and "Dinitiisque" are doubtful as printed; marked [?]. "fera fica" in line 3 is read as "sica" (long s form); the printed letter is not clear, so it is left unmarked. Line breaks within the poem are kept as printed; the poem is set as one block without stanza breaks. Verse lines 1–20 are italic except where roman type appears (HARLÆVS, CORDE, DENTE, IVDAITA, etc., are small capitals and kept as printed).
